1. [Maximum mark: 10]
The function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is defined by
$f(x)=2\mathrm{e}^{x}-\mathrm{e}^{-x}$.
(a) Show that $f$ is a bijection. [4 marks]
(b) Find an expression for $f^{-1}(x)$. [6 marks]

2.text_clean:
2. [Maximum mark: 10]
The relation $R$ is defined for $2\times 2$ matrices such that $\boldsymbol{A}R\boldsymbol{B}$ if and only if there exists a non-singular matrix $\boldsymbol{H}$ such that $\boldsymbol{AH}=\boldsymbol{HB}$.
(a) Show that $R$ is an equivalence relation. [7 marks]
(b) Given that $\boldsymbol{A}$ is singular and $\boldsymbol{A}R\boldsymbol{B}$, show that $\boldsymbol{B}$ is also singular. [3 marks]

3.text_clean:
3. [Maximum mark: 14]
(a) Consider the set $A=\{1, 3, 5, 7\}$ under the binary operation $*$, where $*$ denotes multiplication modulo 8.
(i) Write down the Cayley table for $\{A, *\}$.
(ii) Show that $\{A, *\}$ is a group.
(iii) Find all solutions to the equation $3*x*7=y$. Give your answers in the form $(x, y)$. [9 marks]
(b) Now consider the set $B=\{1, 3, 5, 7, 9\}$ under the binary operation $\otimes$, where $\otimes$ denotes multiplication modulo 10. Show that $\{B, \otimes\}$ is not a group. [2 marks]
(c) Another set $C$ can be formed by removing an element from $B$ so that $\{C, \otimes\}$ is a group.
(i) State which element has to be removed.
(ii) Determine whether or not $\{A, *\}$ and $\{C, \otimes\}$ are isomorphic. [3 marks]

4.text_clean:
4. [Maximum mark: 13]
The permutation $p_1$ of the set $\{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ is defined by
$p_1=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3&4\\2&4&1&3\end{pmatrix}$.
(a) (i) State the inverse of $p_1$.
(ii) Find the order of $p_1$. [5 marks]
(b) Another permutation $p_2$ is defined by
$p_2=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3&4\\3&2&4&1\end{pmatrix}$.
(i) Determine whether or not the composition of $p_1$ and $p_2$ is commutative.
(ii) Find the permutation $p_3$ which satisfies
$p_1p_3p_2=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3&4\\1&2&3&4\end{pmatrix}$. [8 marks]

5.text_clean:
5. [Maximum mark: 13]
Let $G$ be a finite cyclic group.
(a) Prove that $G$ is Abelian. [4 marks]
(b) Given that $a$ is a generator of $G$, show that $a^{-1}$ is also a generator. [5 marks]
(c) Show that if the order of $G$ is five, then all elements of $G$, apart from the identity, are generators of $G$. [4 marks]
